exercise.name: Lever Front Pulldown

reference.title: Lever Front Pulldown
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

equipment: Plate-loaded pulldown machine (iso-lateral lever arms, thigh roller)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull the handles down, breathe in as they rise.
breathing.cadence: About 1.3 s down, short squeeze, about 2 s up

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Plate load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can pull to the upper chest without leaning back.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Sit with the thighs under the roller and the feet flat; reach up and take the handles, palms forward, arms long.
Breathe out and pull the handles down and slightly back toward the upper chest, elbows driving down.
Squeeze the shoulder blades down and together with the hands beside the upper chest.
Breathe in and let the handles rise along their arc until the arms are long.
Let the lats stretch at the top without shrugging.

mistakes.fix: Stay nearly upright; lean back only a little.
Start each rep by drawing the shoulder blades down.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the handles yank the arms up
mistakes.fix: Take about 2 s on the way up.
Keep the shoulders away from the ears.

kinematics.peak: ≈141° with the hands beside the upper chest
kinematics.norm: From nearly straight overhead to well bent beside the chest (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Upper arms down beside the trunk (≈16°)
kinematics.norm: From the arms overhead to the upper arms beside the trunk (clinical opinion)
Pronated: palms forward on horizontal handles (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pivot 145.4 cm high, -86 cm behind the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Lever swings 24.4°; hands within 0.49 cm of the arc
kinematics.norm: The handles ride an arc down and slightly back from a pivot behind the head (clinical opinion)
Front pulldowns load the latissimus dorsi more than behind-the-neck pulldowns (Signorile 2002)

kinematics.setup: Pause 0.5 s with the arms long
kinematics.peak: 1.3 s down, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s up
kinematics.norm: About 1.3 s down and 2 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #5066, Lever Front Pulldown, video (movement reference)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)
Signorile, Zink & Szwed 2002, a comparative electromyographical investigation of muscle utilization patterns using various hand positions during the lat pull-down (J Strength Cond Res 16(4):539-546)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Plate load is user-chosen: start light; keep the thighs under the roller.
Let the handles rise to the stop under control before letting go.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort overhead: stop the handles a little lower at the top.

muscleNotes.lats_r: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm down and back (Lehman 2004; Signorile 2002 for pulldown grips).
